technical-summary: Removed the redundant coding-lsp/usage surface contribution that duplicated the ag-lsp MCP tool list (lsp_symbols, lsp_diagnostics, etc.) into every provider's instruction file. The block was surfaced unconditionally to all providers, but the ag-lsp MCP server is only propagated to providers that don't self-provide LSP (opencode via native pyright language_servers_config, pi via on_lsp_enabled/pi-lens). This caused opencode's AGENTS.md to advertise lsp_* tools the agent didn't actually have, so the agent hunted for them, failed, and fell back to running pyright CLI. Root-cause fix: delete the contribution so the MCP registration is the single source of truth for tool availability — MCP delivers tool names and descriptions to the agent automatically via tools/list, and only to providers that actually receive the server. Usage doctrine remains in each MCP server's instructions field in coding-lsp.yaml. Regenerated provider surfaces (skill_surfaces apply), which pruned the coding-lsp/usage block from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md. No gating mechanism and no native-LSP instruction block were added (chosen approach: omit). Providers unit suite green. Follow-up (not done): the ag-lsp-mgmt harness-instructions block is the same class of MCP-tool duplication and could be reconsidered; and lsp_mcp.py's FastMCP server does not currently pass the coding-lsp.yaml ag-lsp instructions field as server-level instructions.

Updated unit tests (region replacement, empty-removal, legacy migration, prune) and the consistency test (region regex + single-well-formed-region check + legacy-absence). Updated the Docker-gated integration helper managed_blocks_in to map region `## Title` headings back to contribution ids via load_surface_contributions. Regenerated all tracked agent surface files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, COPILOT.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, .clinerules/audiagentic.md, .roo/rules/audiagentic.md) to the new region layout. Behavior note: managed content now consolidates into one contiguous region (moved to end of user-owned files on migration) rather than interleaving. Full unit suite passes.

technical-summary: Fixed a foundation bug: the canonical error type _Error (AudiaGenticError) was a @dataclass(frozen=True) Exception. A frozen dataclass overrides __setattr__ to block all attribute writes, including __traceback__/__cause__/__context__ that Python's exception machinery assigns on raise and during propagation through contextlib with-blocks — producing FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field '__traceback__'. Exposed by the A26 work raising AudiaGenticError through rig contextmanager paths, but latent for all subclasses (LspError/LspServerError inherit the frozen __setattr__, hence their object.__setattr__ workarounds). Changed @dataclass(frozen=True) -> @dataclass(eq=False): exceptions are now mutable enough for the runtime to set traceback/cause/context, while eq=False keeps identity-based equality and hashability (the convention for exceptions; verified nothing hashes or value-compares errors). Verified: raise-through-contextmanager, raise-from chaining, LspError subclass, and __post_init__ code/kind validation all work. Also updated 5 stale assertions in test_embedded_launch.py from pytest.raises(SystemExit) to pytest.raises(AudiaGenticError) to match the A26-converted rig functions. Full tests/unit suite now green (only 2 environment-gated skips); the fix also cleared the workflow-propagation failures that were masked by the same FrozenInstanceError.

technical-summary: Fixed enable_component('coding-lsp') blocking/timing out. The coding-lsp enable lifecycle fires provision_provider_lsp_support, which runs each provider's on_lsp_enabled hook. The only such hook, pi adapter's _pi_ensure_lens, ran `pi install npm:pi-lens` (a network npm install) via subprocess.run with NO timeout, synchronously inside the MCP enable request. Since enable_component writes the enabled marker before firing the event, the component showed enabled while the MCP response blocked on npm, eventually hitting the client request timeout (MCP -32001). Fix: extracted the install into _install_pi_lens(pi_bin) (subprocess.run with timeout=300, logs non-zero/errors) and dispatched it on a background daemon thread from _pi_ensure_lens, which now returns immediately ({ok, started, detail}). Enabling no longer blocks on the install (best-effort, idempotent). Measured provision time dropped from 3.64s to 0.03s. Updated tests: split into test_ensure_lens_starts_background_install_when_harness_present (asserts non-blocking dispatch to _install_pi_lens with pi_bin) and test_install_pi_lens_runs_install_command (asserts the install command); skip-when-absent test unchanged. coding_lsp + providers unit suites green; Ruff clean. Not a bug (diagnosed for the user): the ag-lsp generic MCP is correctly projected only to providers that do NOT self-provide LSP (present in .mcp.json); native-LSP providers like opencode get native lsp config instead, which requires enabling a language.

No index file (deterministic shard paths via glob). No per-shard locking (out of scope; codebase relies on atomic replace). All public accessor signatures unchanged so the ~10 consumer files need no edits. Added migration test and isolation test. Validated host + inside Docker image audiagentic-test (12 foundation tests pass); provider+lsp unit suites green; ruff clean on changed files.
